entities.name: Battle of Dandanaqan
entities.label: EventWindow
entities.summary:
The Battle of Dandanaqan was a pivotal event in 1040, marking a key turning point in the Seljuk-Ghaznavid Wars. Taking place on May 29, 1040, in the city of Merv, this battle saw the Seljuk Turks emerge victorious against the Ghaznavid Empire, paving the way for the Turks' eventual rise to power in the region.

The core events of the battle involved the Seljuk forces, led by Chaghri Beg and his brother Tughrul, who decisively defeated the Ghaznavid army. This victory not only secured the Turks' control over the region but also had significant consequences for the subsequent history of the area.

The legacy of the Battle of Dandanaqan can be seen in the eventual establishment of the Seljuk Empire, which went on to play a crucial role in shaping the political landscape of the Middle East. Its impact was felt for centuries to come, with the empire's influence extending beyond its borders to affect the course of world history.

As the renowned historian, Ibn al-Athir, noted, 'The Battle of Dandanaqan was a turning point in the history of the Turks, marking the beginning of their rise to power in the region.'
